task: Add pair 4 to §4 of docs/research/W2-108-freshness-once.md, correct the sentences saying no run reached a load of 40, review the verdict on query-embedding batching against all eight runs, commit the record alone, and run the acceptance tests once more.
status: DONE — the record is committed on its own; the acceptance tests give 26 passed, 1 skipped.
work_completed: §4 now covers pair 4 in its method (four pairs, the order of the runs, pair 4's times), its table (two new rows, plus a 5-minute load column, "—" for pairs 1–3) and its findings. The "load" paragraph is rewritten: pairs 1–3 never reached 40, pair 4 did with both runs, but its two runs were about 15 apart in load. The verdict is reviewed against all eight runs. I changed nothing outside §4.

evidence: Commit 2e694819da0f, with the trailers Task: DAEO-zoex, Role: engineer, Implements: DEC-969, Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. `git log --oneline -2` shows 2e694819, then e8f959a1 (the lead's checkpoint). `git diff --numstat HEAD~1 HEAD` shows one file, +81 −45. `git status --short` shows only the same untracked dotfiles at the root, which are not mine. The hooks folder holds only `*.sample` files. Before editing, I checked that the record had not changed since f34afb5e61b6.
tests: tests/acceptance/W2-108, run once after the commit: 26 passed, 1 skipped (test_w2_108_unchanged.py:140: "the semantic facet of /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-108 is unavailable here (stale): no embedder answers, or the store holds no current vectors"). No unit suites were run, since no code changed.
discoveries: At a mean load of 48 (after-4), the run without any of its query-embedding time would still take 612 s, over 600. So no amount of batching can bring that run under the limit. The part of the run outside the freshness checks and query embedding grew to 593 s in after-4 (550 s in after-1). That part is now the largest cost at heavy load, and this measure does not break it down.
risks: Pair 4's wall-time saving (1,351 s) mixes the change with a 15-point fall in load; the record says so. The figures for the freshness checks are the clean comparison. All wall times include cProfile's overhead. Pair 4's call counts and `_checked` times were not given, so the record cites those for pairs 1–3 only.
lessons: When a new pair is added, every sentence that ranged over "all runs" has to be found and either rescoped or corrected. A search over the section for "No run", "heaviest" and "either load" found them.
proposed_decisions: The verdict on option (b), for the owner (DEC-969):
- **At means of about 10 and 20:** batching is not needed. The check is already under 600 s (300 s and 406 s).
- **At means of 36 and 48:** batching is not enough on its own. After-1 would need its 373 s of embedding cut to under 33 s. After-4 stays at 612 s even with no embedding time at all.
- **What batching could do:** shorten heavy-load runs, since embedding is 40–42 % of them. The figures don't show by how much.
- **What decides the limit at heavy load:** the unattributed rest of the run (550–593 s).

My confidence is high for what the figures exclude, and low for what batching would save.
unresolved: Two things are not attributed: what fills the rest of the run at heavy load (550–593 s outside the two measured parts), and how much of each wall time is cProfile's overhead. Whether pair 4's 15-point gap between its runs satisfies KPI 4's "at the same measured load" is the lead's call; the record states the gap.
recommended_next_action: The lead does the scoped verification and returns to the orchestrator. The orchestrator brings the owner the verdict on option (b), and the finding that at heavy load the cost is outside freshness checking and query embedding.
